done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. `TEST_NAME` recognizes only Python `test_*.py` and `*_test.py` files, so `proof_list` copies a line naming a JavaScript test unchanged when `names` is empty. A default stack client runs `npm test` and Playwright (`src/forge/templates/conventions/testing.md:11,20`); if its worker names a nonexistent or unrun `.test.ts` or `.spec.ts` test, Close publishes that name without checking its run. The new command tests cover only pytest names.
findings.title: Close leaves JavaScript test names unchecked in client proof lists

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. This command-level proof checks only the `passed` result. There is no assertion that a named test which fails in Close's run appears as `failed` in the published pull request. The test would still pass if `proof_list` labeled every reported test as passed, leaving the Done-when requirement to publish test results unproven for a normal failed run.
findings.title: Not done: a failed named test is published as failed

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
